post_stop_loss_continuation.reason: The active goal resumed automatically, allowing narrowly scoped checks of the pinned release's native browser path and the localized portal failure.
post_stop_loss_continuation.result: No screenshot; the additional paths converged on the same unaccelerated guest-browser blocker.

resolution.strategy: Replace only the redundant amd64 outer host with a digest-pinned native ARM64 QEMU-Docker derivative; retain the pinned x86_64 OSWorld guest unchanged.
resolution.result: The public PixelGym reset returned a stable 1920x1080 uint8 screenshot after expanding the ephemeral guest root to 48.5 GiB (20.4 GiB free) and closed its provider cleanly. The measured expanded reset took 183.2311019160552 seconds.

resolved_diagnostics.observation: The upstream provider called psutil.net_connections(), which raised AccessDenied on macOS.
resolved_diagnostics.resolution: The adapter now uses a Darwin-only socket bind plus Docker port-map check before provider startup.

resolved_diagnostics.observation: The guest service initially killed its own cleanup shell because the pkill pattern matched the shell command.
resolved_diagnostics.resolution: Cleanup uses self-excluding process patterns; the guest service starts, answers readiness, resets atomically, and returns the expected task identity.

resolved_diagnostics.observation: The screenshot endpoint and wmctrl window-manager probe become ready under software emulation.
resolved_diagnostics.resolution: Task setup now waits explicitly for the window manager before browser launch.

resolved_diagnostics.observation: OSWorld's SetupController caches transfers by source URL, so a stable task-ID filename reused an older bundle after task-app code changed.
resolved_diagnostics.resolution: Guest bundle filenames now include the first 16 hexadecimal characters of the exact bundle SHA-256; the task ID and bundle content remain independently deterministic.

resolved_diagnostics.observation: The pinned QCOW2 advertised a 50 GiB virtual disk, but its root partition had not consumed the available virtual capacity and Ubuntu displayed a low-disk notification during the first long trajectory.
resolved_diagnostics.resolution: The adapter now requests OSWorld's 50 GB volume expansion for each ephemeral snapshot. The verified root is 48.5 GiB with 20.4 GiB free; the replacement 112-step trajectory had no low-disk notification.

final_blocker.observation: Chrome never created a visible client window or posted the task-bound /api/page-ready marker. Direct launches showed D-Bus StartServiceByName NoReply, xdg-desktop-portal activation timeouts, FUSE permission errors for /run/user/1000 portal mounts, and libva/DRI authentication failures. The release-native CDP path returned ECONNRESET for all 15 retries even after the window manager was ready. The release-native recovery command kept Chrome, zygote, and GPU processes alive but still created no X11 client window. A private bus without service activation instead drove the guest to a one-core CPU spin and made its control endpoint unresponsive.
focused_variants_tested: private bus with GTK/GIO portal opt-out and basic password store
release-native chrome_open_tabs after explicit desktop readiness
private session bus with no service-activation directories
final_blocker.interpretation: The pinned x86-64 guest boots on the arm64 Docker engine without KVM, but its desktop portal/browser startup is not viable enough to produce the required real screenshot within the bounded local investigation. The core Gym contract was not changed to accommodate this provider behavior.

next_provider_gate: Resolved locally by the recorded native ARM64 compatibility host; the inspected ARM64 UTM VM is not needed.
